name: Boti Kebab
subtitle: yogurt-marinated mutton cubes, charred outside and juicy through

ingredients.note: thin yogurt slides off the meat
tenderiser; skip only if using very young goat

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp, heated to smoking and cooled

ingredients.note: stops the yogurt from weeping in the heat

prepNotes: Marinate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, refrigerated. Under 2 hours and the mutton stays tough.
Take the meat out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking so it grills evenly.
Roast the besan in a dry pan until it smells nutty and cool it before it goes near the yogurt.

steps.text: Pat the mutton cubes completely dry and prick each one two or three times with a fork.
Rub in the papaya paste, ginger, garlic and salt and leave 20 minutes.
Whisk the hung yogurt with the roasted besan, kashmiri chilli, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper and the cooled mustard oil until smooth.
steps.tip: Smoked-then-cooled mustard oil loses its raw bite but keeps the pungency.

steps.text: Fold the meat through the marinade, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Thread onto skewers with a finger gap between cubes so the heat gets all the way round.
steps.tip: Packed tight, they steam instead of charring.

steps.text: Grill over medium-hot charcoal or under an oven grill at 240C for 12–15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes.
Baste with ghee in the last 4 minutes and let the edges blacken in patches.
Rest 3 minutes off the heat, then dust with chaat masala and squeeze over lemon.
steps.tip: Resting lets the juices settle; cut one straight away and it bleeds out.

storage: Eat within the hour. Marinated raw meat keeps 2 days refrigerated. Leftover cooked boti is best chopped into a paratha roll rather than reheated whole.
